requirement: Criterion code uses {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read` for this operation.
rationale:
The subject `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_node.fn` has one obligation. Criterion code reads a node through `ValidationContext.read`, and that operation is specified by the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read`. The subject adds no input classes, boundaries or failure modes of its own. Its testable content is that the public `read(&self, node) -> Result<NodeContent, Error>` operation exists and works for criterion code.

The implementation is `ValidationContext::read` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[ValidationContext<'d, D>]#2/fn[read]`. It has the required signature and delegates to `read_snapshot`. I read it only to confirm which item the {impl} reference marks.

The marked test is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[direct_reads_return_complete_unicode_contents_and_snapshots]`. It calls `inspection.read(&1)` through the public API, the way criterion code would.
- **Success case:** for both an empty string and a large multi-byte Unicode string, it asserts that `read` returns the exact contents. It asserts that the returned contents stay unchanged after the underlying graph is mutated. It asserts that the dependency recorded is `Dependency::Node(1, fp(original))`. It asserts that the graph was read the expected number of times.
- **Failure case:** a `read(&9)` of a missing node returns the error `"missing"` and records no dependency.

These assertions enforce the observable behavior of the operation the subject points criterion code to. The behavior and inputs of `read` are covered by the cited and sibling requirements, so I did not reassess them here. I found no gap.

The tool reads a known node, such as the current node or a target from `outgoing_edges`.
Each page’s `text` contains the next portion of the node’s formatted contents. Formatting follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.judge.rendering`.
:::{req} read_node.fn
Criterion code uses {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.ValidationContext.read` for this operation.
:::{req} read_node.inputs
A successful `ValidationContext::read` records the node's identity and the
fingerprint of the returned contents, under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.node_inputs`. A failed read records no
successful observation. The evidence becomes stale when a later read of that
node has a different fingerprint; a failure to resolve it is reported by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`.
For a Rust caller, the SDK records the fingerprint when `read` returns the
contents. For an agent, the harness puts a tool result in the next request to
the model and records the fingerprint once the provider responds successfully.
That successful exchange is *delivery*. For example, suppose the tool reads a
function that returns `3`, and someone changes it to return `4` before the
provider responds. The model saw the version that returns `3`, so the SDK
records the fingerprint it computed from that version. Reading the function
again at this point would record a fingerprint for code the model never saw.
:::{req} read_node.mcp

text remains, pass `next` to `get_next_page`.
